title: Testing bipartiteness in bounded-degree graphs

problem.name: Testing bipartiteness in bounded-degree graphs
problem.statement_latex:
For a graph of maximum degree $d=O(1)$, distinguish a bipartite graph from one requiring more than $\varepsilon dn$ edge changes to become bipartite. Neighbor-list queries give the $j$th neighbor of a specified vertex. The promise permits sublinear property testing.
Complexity counts neighbor-oracle queries and running time for fixed maximum degree and fixed distance parameter.
problem.statement_text: For a graph of maximum degree $d=O(1)$, distinguish a bipartite graph from one requiring more than $\varepsilon dn$ edge changes to become bipartite. Neighbor-list queries give the $j$th neighbor of a specified vertex. The promise permits sublinear property testing. Complexity counts neighbor-oracle queries and running time for fixed maximum degree and fixed distance parameter.

quantum.details_latex: The theorem assumes fixed $d$ and $\varepsilon$. Reversible random-walk generation and quantum collision finding locate opposite-parity walks with a common endpoint. The decision has bounded error, with one-sided acceptance for bipartite graphs.
quantum.details_text: The theorem assumes fixed $d$ and $\varepsilon$. Reversible random-walk generation and quantum collision finding locate opposite-parity walks with a common endpoint. The decision has bounded error, with one-sided acceptance for bipartite graphs.

classical.details_latex: The tester samples walks from chosen starting vertices and detects an odd-cycle certificate from conflicting parities. The lower bound applies to the same bounded-degree property-testing promise. Dependence on $d$, $\varepsilon$ and confidence is restored when these parameters vary with $n$.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial: $\sqrt n\to\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$, through collision-finding quantum walks.
strength.description_text: Polynomial: $\sqrt n\to\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$, through collision-finding quantum walks.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous advantage over a classical property-testing lower bound.
evidence.description_text: Rigorous advantage over a classical property-testing lower bound.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant neighbor queries and reversible walk generation are needed. A direct collision-finding implementation stores $\widetilde O(n^{1/3})$ bits of walk seeds and endpoints in the fixed-parameter regime, in addition to oracle workspace.
